old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a small, intricate mechanical device placed on a wooden base with a green mat underneath. The device features a central circular component with a blue propeller attached to it, spinning rapidly. A person's arm, clad in a textured beige sweater, is partially visible on the left side, holding a white object that appears to be a remote control or a similar device. The arm moves the object towards the spinning propeller, but the propeller continues spinning without stopping. The background is a plain black, which contrasts sharply with the bright blue of the propeller and the metallic sheen of the central component. The lighting is focused on the device, highlighting its details and the motion of the spinning propeller. The scene remains static except for the movement of the arm and the propeller, creating a sense of controlled energy and precision.

caption: The video captures a tabletop apparatus: a clear acrylic stand with two angled support posts holds a vertically mounted spiral coil of concentric rings on a central pivot. It rests on a white plate atop a green mat and wooden board, set against a black backdrop with a gray wall at right. A bright blue rod fixed at the pivot spins continuously, appearing in each frame as a blurred radial streak that points successively left, upward, rightward, and downward, cycling around the center. A white curved arc sweeps around the coil in step with the streak. The coil, posts, base, and background remain fixed while the camera stays still. At the left edge a person's light-colored sleeve and blurred hand appear; the hand moves in and out of view during the early frames, after which only the sleeve remains. The rotation is already underway at the first frame and continues through the last, neither starting nor stopping within the clip.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

review_issues.quote: A faint white curved trail sweeps in step with the streak, marking its path around the coil.
review_issues.problem: The white arc consistently sits about a quarter-turn ahead of the blue streak (e.g., streak left / arc top; streak up / arc right), so it does not trail behind or mark the streak's path; calling it a 'trail' is unsupported.

review_issues.quote: the hand withdraws out of view during the early frames, leaving only the sleeve.
review_issues.problem: The hand is not withdrawn once; it reappears at the left edge in several early frames (around the sixth and seventh views) before finally disappearing, so a single withdrawal leaving only the sleeve is inaccurate.
